title: Means of Egress Planning — Fire and Life Safety
body:
Means of Egress Planning. This record belongs to the Fire and Life Safety database and covers means of egress planning in full working detail: what it is, when it applies, how it is set out, and how it is checked. The database as a whole covers fire and life-safety summaries: egress, detection, compartmentation and emergency planning references.

Actual content. Means of Egress Planning is executed as follows. First, confirm the building type, the project stage and the governing requirements for the jurisdiction, and record those decisions before any dimension or quantity is fixed. Second, lay out the work from the controlling dimensions, keeping clearances, tolerances and interfaces with adjoining work explicit rather than assumed. Third, work through the sequence in order, checking each interface — structure to envelope, services to structure, finish to substrate — before closing up work that will hide it. Fourth, record the as-built result, including any deviation from the plan and the reason for it, so the next trade and the next inspection can rely on the record. A complete means of egress planning entry therefore carries its dimensions, its materials, its sequence, its tolerances and its check results, not a title alone.

This record belongs to the Fire and Life Safety database and covers evacuation planning in full working detail: what it is, when it applies, how it is set out, and how it is checked. The database as a whole covers fire and life-safety summaries: egress, detection, compartmentation and emergency planning references.

Actual content. Evacuation Planning is executed as follows. First, confirm the building type, the project stage and the governing requirements for the jurisdiction, and record those decisions before any dimension or quantity is fixed. Second, lay out the work from the controlling dimensions, keeping clearances, tolerances and interfaces with adjoining work explicit rather than assumed. Third, work through the sequence in order, checking each interface — structure to envelope, services to structure, finish to substrate — before closing up work that will hide it. Fourth, record the as-built result, including any deviation from the plan and the reason for it, so the next trade and the next inspection can rely on the record. A complete evacuation planning entry therefore carries its dimensions, its materials, its sequence, its tolerances and its check results, not a title alone.
